questions.text: I detect when someone is watching a conversation from the periphery with more interest than they are showing.
I often feel like my emotional responses are running at double speed compared to the people around me.
I would describe my influence style as directive.
I prefer the group to decide together when a project is truly complete.
I can usually tell when someone has been crying even if they have composed themselves.
Learning that suffering could easily be prevented seldom makes me want it prevented.
I design my workflows to minimize friction and maximize repeatability.
When I see an opportunity, I move quickly to claim it.
I experience the conclusion of something I care about with a sense of readiness to move on.
I take a methodical approach to learning new skills, following a structured curriculum.
Most of the time, other people's suffering does not feel important to me.
I would share a professional secret or competitive advantage if it would significantly help someone else.
I am typically the one who helps the group keep deliberating until a tie resolves itself.
When I feel truly heard and understood, the relief is so profound it can make me cry.
A person's suffering still matters to me when many other people also know about it.
Learning that a person is suffering makes me want to know if there is anything that would help them.
As I learn the reasons a person is struggling, their wellbeing becomes more important to me.
When someone near me is visibly upset, I rarely feel any urge to comfort or help them.
I tend to feel the same emotional temperature whether I'm at home or in a novel situation.
I do regular tasks when I remember them rather than relying on calendar prompts.
I routinely protect my focus time even when others express disappointment.
I rotate seasonal items in and out of storage on a predictable schedule.
I tend to treat silence in a conversation as simply a pause rather than as communication.
I can look back on difficult periods without re-experiencing the emotional intensity.
I tend to schedule personal time before committing to obligations for others.
I notice that when I feel vulnerable, every nerve ending seems to be exposed.
I routinely decline social events that don't advance my personal interests.
I tend to be unaware of the unspoken rules about what topics are acceptable at a particular gathering.
I tend to miss it when a person's agreement comes with a subtle qualifier that changes its meaning entirely.
I notice when a group conversation has an unacknowledged moderator who is guiding the flow without being explicit about it.
I tend to go without rest to make sure the people around me are supported.
I routinely make financial sacrifices to support people in my life.
I feel uncomfortable when someone challenges my authority in front of the group.
I hold my commitments loosely, knowing that priorities shift and flexibility matters.
I handle errands and tasks as they come up, even if that means extra trips.
When a conversation stalls, I invite quieter voices to share before proposing anything.
